_source_of_truth: EDIT THIS FILE. `LEDGER.md` and `ledger.html` are GENERATED views — never hand-edit them; run `npm run ledger` (pre-commit also regenerates). Schema + workflow: README.md in this folder.
ledgerPhilosophy: EPHEMERAL working state, not history. Applied findings are DELETED (git + the commit message are the fix record), never stamped done. Keep only open/later rows + skip-tombstones.
_findingSchema: each finding: { id, dim, bucket, verdict, status, finding } + optional `pattern` — a one-line positive exemplar (the good pattern to follow), not just the problem. The loop's own anti-negative-instruction principle: state the target behavior, not only the prohibition. Full schema: README.md.

findings.finding: plugin/commands/contribute.md (SHIPPED) is still built on the dead two-tree model: it stages domains/<name>/plugin/{skills,library}/ and its scope-safety rule forbids staging plugin/ (CORE) — but promote-run.js locate() lands promotions in plugin/{skills,library}/ (one tree). A path fix collapses the command's own safety rule, so it needs a redesign: distinguish contributable learnings from CORE by git history / promotions-board provenance instead of by path. Found 2026-07-24 while applying D7-suite-godot-stale.
findings.pattern: promote-run.js is the source of truth for where capabilities land; commands describe ITS behavior, not a remembered layout.

findings.finding: ui/server/features/skills/skill-scope.js (+ skill-scope.check.js) still models the godot {genre, style} game-profile filter with godot-* skill examples baked into comments and the check fixtures (godot-core, style-pixel, genre-fps). The MECHANISM (domain-tag filtering of an agent's preload list) is generic and possibly useful per-domain; the vocabulary is engine payload. Decide: re-parameterize profiles per domain pack (domain.json could declare its own profile axes) or strip the profile filter until a second domain needs it. Found 2026-07-24 recalibration sweep.
findings.pattern: generic mechanism, domain vocabulary — the axes a profile filters on should come from the domain descriptor, not hardcoded genre/style.

findings.finding: MEASURED this pass: the observe+score hook IS restored and wired (plugin/hooks/caveman-reminder.sh, hooks.json:71) and logs/caveman-gate.log holds 2378 rows — marker:true 23 (0.97%), verbose:true 168 (7%). Sub-agent TERSENESS holds (~93% non-verbose) while the [cvmn] marker is effectively never emitted. Decide: drop the marker convention from caveman-forge + the agent prompts (it costs prompt space and a per-tool-call hook nudge for ~1% compliance), or enforce it deterministically. Caveat: rows repeat per tool call, so the ratio is directional, not per-message.

findings.finding: Xenomoon now diverges from xenodot on more than identity: renamed roster (product-owner), fork-only tools (mcp__ui__epic), fork-only skills (grill, xeno-epic), fork-only process docs (skill-writing). No systematic check that these divergent surfaces are wired everywhere xenodot's originals were (hooks matchers, skill-catalog derivations, templates, first-boot copy, /sync-upstream seam list) — each landed by hand-grep. Add the fork-divergent surfaces to docs/fork/SEAMS.md so /sync-upstream and the audit suite treat them as first-class seams instead of rediscovering them per session. FIRST LIVE BITE (2026-07-30, fixed 376c614): trunk tracked plugin/library/sources/skill-sources.md — a path webapp-pack installs WRITE untracked — breaking `xenomoon update` in every bound clone; invariant extracted: the trunk never tracks a path a domain-pack install writes (audit should CHECK trunk-tracked paths against every pack's install file list).
findings.pattern: every fork-divergent surface is a named seam in SEAMS.md — sync and audit read the list, not the diff.

findings.finding: agent-report/SKILL.md:31 contracts the relayed result to '<path> — gate PASS|FAIL' but nothing enforces it — no SubagentStop hook anywhere (verified 2026-07-08); review measured ~1.2k-char avg prose results vs the ~50-char contract; harden: SubagentStop regex validator + digest cap ≤6 lines (review P0B-3 merged schema).

That same record (Clerk/EAS/TestFlight/Play traps) is Expo-mobile PAYLOAD sitting in the GENERIC CORE library, and it is untracked — so it ships to nobody while polluting the neutral tier. Second-domain test: a webapp install gets a Play-Console/EAS record it can never use. Fix: move it to domains/expoapp/plugin/library/findings/ with its index line, and commit it there.

The fork-sync-upstream skill is SELF-DECLARED domain-agnostic (its description: "Written platform-neutral; promotable out of this domain"; expoapp/orchestrator.md:52 calls it "a standing promotion candidate for the CORE plugin") yet lives inside domains/expoapp — a webapp-domain fork cannot reach it. Dependency-direction inversion: the generic capability is trapped under one domain. Fix: promote to CORE plugin/skills/ (human-gated promotion).

token-audit exists as two diverged copies of one command: plugin/commands/token-audit.md (1715 w, $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT paths) and .claude/commands/token-audit.md (2309 w, .claude/ paths) — the shipped copy lacks the "Domain separation" + "Do this" sections and the entire history.json / `npm run token-history` half, with nothing keeping them in sync. Decide: the shipped copy declares the forge revision it was ported from, or one is generated from the other.

update-badges.js counts the FILESYSTEM plugin tree, which after a local `forge new` includes the installed pack that the trunk deliberately does not track — so the pre-commit hook rewrote README.md + .claude-plugin/marketplace.json to Skills 20 / Agents 7 while the repo actually ships 13 / 5. The published numbers describe one machine s install state, and no gate catches it (validate skips badges by design). Fix: count git-TRACKED plugin files (git ls-files plugin/{skills,agents}) so install output cannot inflate what the repo advertises. Accepted knowingly in the 2026-08-13 audit-fix commit.
findings.pattern: a derived artifact that SHIPS is computed from what the repo tracks, never from what happens to be on disk.

findings.finding: The invariant "the trunk never tracks a path a domain-pack install writes" is ALREADY violated beyond the skill-sources case: domains/webapp/plugin/hooks/hooks.json installs to plugin/hooks/hooks.json, which CORE tracks (12 tracked files in plugin/hooks/). Installing webapp would clobber a tracked file and break `xenomoon update` exactly as 376c614 did — unnoticed only because webapp has not been installed here. The invariant is prose in framework-sources.md with no mechanical guard. Fix: a check:* that diffs every pack s install file list against `git ls-files plugin/` and fails on any overlap (the audit-suite check D10-fork-divergence-wiring already asked for), plus decide per collision whether the path is CORE-owned or pack-owned (hooks.json needs a merge strategy, not an overwrite).
findings.pattern: a pack install path and a trunk-tracked path are disjoint sets, enforced by a gate — not by remembering.
